title: Introduce inference telemetry conductor and strand metrics
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Motivation: long-tail cost/latency regressions are often visible only when looking at fine-grained per-token and per-phase behavior across invocations. Existing rollups blur phase boundaries (prefetch, decode, kv-lookup, kernel-exec) and make it hard to attribute cost spikes to kernel contention, cache misses, or prompt shape. This PR introduces the "Telemetry Conductor": a lightweight inference-side router that emits 'strand' level metrics (a strand is a contiguous phase slice of an invocation) and enriches spans with strand metadata for high-fidelity attribution. Design summary: the conductor tags each invocation with a strand_id and strand_phase labels, aggregates micro-rollups per-strand (token_count, token_cost_ns, kernel_ms, kv_hits), and emits compact histograms and counters to our metrics backend. Traces are enriched with strand metadata via span attributes and a small span synthesizer that links sampled spans to the strand rollups. To limit cardinality, we hash tenant_id and quantization bins into stable labels and apply a controlled sampling policy: default 1% global sampling, automatic ramp to 10-20% for invocations flagged by SLO anomalies. New metrics exported: strand_latency_ms_bucket, strand_token_cost_sum, strand_token_cost_count, strand_kernel_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99 (as summaries), strand_cache_hit_ratio_gauge, strand_batch_size_gauge, strand_quant_level_label (low/med/high). Dashboards: added a dedicated Strand Metrics dashboard that surfaces per-route strand composition, kernel-level cost maps, and a 'Cost Micro-Atlas' panel that slices tenant-level spend by strand phase and kernel. Also added an alert tuning guide that suggests per-route thresholds and a cost-stability SLO tied to strand_token_cost_count histogram shifts. Backwards compatibility and rollout: integration is opt-in via feature-flag (telemetry.conductor.enabled) and uses a non-blocking path so there is negligible latency impact when disabled. When enabled, conductor runs inline but uses batching and async flushes to avoid tail amplification; perf microbench shows ~1.8% median latency overhead at p95 traffic and an acceptable 6% p95 CPU overhead during warmup. Tests: unit tests for conductor router, integration tests for trace enrichment and histogram correctness, end-to-end perf bench included under perf/bench/strand. Migration and storage: metrics are emitted under a new namespace telemetry.strand.*; retention and rollup rules are added to observability/metrics-policy to avoid long-term cardinality growth. Deployment plan: staged, feature-flag gated rollout across prod clusters: canary (10% traffic in 3 regions) -> ramp (40%) -> global enable. Monitor cost delta for first 72 hours; automatic kill-switch if telemetry pipeline error rate >1% or customer-visible latency SLO breaches. Checklist: 1) implement runtime tagging and metric emissions (done), 2) trace enrichment and span synthesizer (done), 3) dashboards and runbook (done), 4) perf/regression benchmarks (done), 5) docs and upgrade notes (docs added), 6) post-merge monitoring playbook (linked in runbook). Related work: follows ENG-847 and builds on prior token-attribution work but differs by providing per-phase "strand" rollups and an event-driven conductor rather than full session reassembly. Risks and mitigations: cardinality risk mitigated via hashed tenant label and bunched quantization; cost overhead mitigated via async batching and aggressive sampling; alert noise addressed by auto-suppressing low-volume tenants and providing a quiet-window option. Merge notes: squash-merged after addressing nits listed below.

feat(metrics): export strand micro-rollups and histograms
chore(dashboards): add strand metrics dashboard and panels

test: add unit + integration tests for strand metrics
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can we avoid adding tenant_id as a raw label? We should hash and prefix to keep cardinality low.
Aisha Kaur: Answered - tenant_id is hashed and we prefix with tenant_h to make it stable across rollups and avoid raw PII.
Lena Park: The sampling ramp to 20% worries me for high-traffic tenants; can we cap by tenant?
Aisha Kaur: Updated to include per-tenant cap (default cap 5%) and a global emergency ramp for SLO-critical anomalies only.
Omar Khalid: Perf numbers look fine but add a smoke test for the async flush path to catch dropped metrics on shutdown.
Aisha Kaur: Added smoke test and improved shutdown flush to block up to 250ms to reduce drop rate.
Miguel Santos: nits on variable names and a suggested small refactor to the exporter to reduce heap churn.
Aisha Kaur: Refactored exporter per suggestion; heap churn reduced in perf bench by ~12%.
Lena Park: Please add a short playbook for investigating strand cost spikes (linked dashboards + key queries).
Aisha Kaur: Playbook added to docs/observability/strand-metrics.md under the Investigations section.
release_notes: Introduce 'Telemetry Conductor' and Strand Metrics: per-invocation strand rollups, trace enrichment, new Strand Metrics dashboard, opt-in feature-flag rollout, and playbook for investigating strand-level cost/latency spikes; default sampling ensures low cardinality and a per-tenant cap is enforced.
